verdict: The typesetting is designed; the pages are still assembled. Home stacks four registers down one unvarying left margin — eyebrow row, 44pt headline, 76pt numeral, table — so no single object owns the page, and the lower 40% is unshaped void with a floating utility pill rather than composed whitespace; the evening screen runs five grammars (ledger, chips, a second headline, a prompt, a form field) on one sheet, which is exactly what Journal would never ship. The onboarding already holds the bar this app is chasing: beat 13's full-bleed plate with the 80pt "500" set into a rising panel, and beat 19's receipt ledger, are Invites-grade one-object compositions — the tabs simply haven't adopted their law. Calibration: the 860 numeral with its italic caption, the bubble-less chat typesetting, and the becoming cover's top third are already publication-quality material; what's missing is composition, scale hierarchy, and imagery, not craft.

compositions.composition: One-hero law, two day registers. Masthead: date folio alone at 13pt tracked caps, nothing else above the fold line. Before the first plate lands, the KEPT LINE owns the page: 64–72pt serif across two stacked lines with the italic punch word, a full-measure hairline drawn beneath it, the hollow ✦ seal sitting ON the rule at its right end like a signature line on a contract, the sub-line beneath as one quiet 17pt sentence; tapping the line opens the camera. After a log lands, the registers swap: "860" at 96pt with italic "calories" becomes the page object (the LANDED silk sweep already built), and the kept line retires to a kept receipt row. Everything else on the page is ONE ledger in onboarding beat-19 grammar — calories, protein, overnight fast, steps as caption-left / 26–34pt serif answer-right rows. The bottom void gets shaped by the ledger's rhythm ending in a foot folio; never two headlines on the sheet.

The close is a ceremony in three acts, top to bottom, one grammar. Act 1: "closing the day." at 64pt. Act 2: the receipt — protein 62 of 90g, plates, steps, tomorrow: a balanced day — as the same caption/answer ledger rows as morning, hairlines only. Act 3: "how did today feel?" at 30pt italic serif, then proud · okay · tender as three bare 38pt serif words spread across the measure; the chosen word inks in deep rose and takes the terminal ♥, and the page is signed. Delete the text field and the second kept line entirely; the evening page closes the day, it does not reopen it. As the acts complete, the page's ink ratio deepens toward deep rose — the evening tint comes from content, the Invites way.

The cover gets cover art. Her best plate photo of the week runs full-bleed through the top 55% (real user photography, used editorially), cream scrim rising from its foot; "becoming" sits INTO the photo top-left as a small cream italic folio; below the scrim line: WEEK 2 OF 20 · FINDING STEADY eyebrow, then the week's thesis at 64–72pt over three stacked lines ("this week: / protein earlier / in the day."), then the cycle note and "talk it through ↗" as the quiet foot. No plates logged yet → the jkDawn shader arc becomes the cover plate instead, so the empty state reads as an invitation, never absence. Fore-edge ticks move to the right screen edge, vertical, 12pt. No hamburger on a book cover.

One figure per spread, set like a plate section in a printed monograph. Each interior page: eyebrow folio at top, then ONE enormous figure — the mounds, the trend canvas, the seven-night band — drawn in ink and rose on cream at 50–60% of page height, then the headline BELOW the figure at 44–52pt (caption-as-headline), one 20pt body line, folio at the foot. The figure is the page; the text captions it. Any spread whose figure cannot hold 55% of the height merges into another spread — a magazine cuts pages before it shrinks pictures. All spreads share one baseline grid so headlines land on identical baselines page after page.

A correspondence, not a console. The day opens with a letterhead: MONDAY in tracked Fraunces caps over a hairline, once per day. jeni's paragraphs set 22–24pt at 1.5 leading; her lines right-set in deep-rose italic serif — her voice printed, not typed. Speaker rhythm 44pt / paragraph rhythm 12pt. The input loses its rounded border: a single hairline UNDER the text like a signature line, "talk to jeni…" as an italic serif ghost, send as an ink ✦ that fills when text exists. The duplicated exchange and the ghost "today" overlap are pulled — in this grammar every seam reads as a misprint.

checklist_iconic.diagnosis: The kept line is beautiful typesetting, not yet an object. It sits at 44pt in the same left column as a 76pt numeral, two meta lines and a table, so the page has no single owner; its hairline reads as a text underline rather than a drawn thing; the ✦ seal floats detached in the right margin instead of belonging to the line; the camera action it implies lives elsewhere, in a FAB; and the whole motif repeats on the evening screen at lower contrast, which breaks the singular. A screenshot of this page is a screenshot of a nice column — nothing in its geometry says THIS is the app.
checklist_iconic.proposal: Make it THE SIGNED LINE — a contract line, one per day. Composition: the 64–72pt two-line serif statement; beneath it a full-measure hairline that is visibly DRAWN (animates left→right on page-in); the hollow ✦ seal sits ON the rule at its right end, exactly where a signature sits; the date prints beneath in 13pt caps as the countersign. The line itself is the tap target — touching it opens the camera; no disc, no chevron. When she keeps it, the seal fills with deep-rose ink under the existing silk sweep and haptic swell, and the sub-line reprints as the receipt: "kept · 6:42pm". The screenshot becomes: a cream page, one enormous sentence, one inked rule, one filled ✦ — an image no other app produces, buildable entirely from the locked hairline, serif, and seal.

becoming_pageturn: Print register first, motion second. All spreads share one baseline grid and folio position, so every turn lands type in the same place — register consistency is what reads as \"printed,\" more than any effect. Then the turn itself, all SwiftUI: ScrollView(.horizontal) with .scrollTargetBehavior(.paging); each page uses .scrollTransition/.visualEffect so the outgoing text block translates at ~0.85x of scroll (the ink pulls back) while a 24pt cream gutter carrying a faint spine shadow (4% cocoa radial gradient) moves at ~1.15x (the paper edge lifting); the incoming headline settles on a spring delayed ~40ms after the page body — ink lands after paper. The right-edge fore-edge ticks decrement as she turns (the book thinning), folio numerals cross-fade \"02 · protein\" → \"03 · sleep\", and each landed page fires one sharp-then-soft haptic detent, a page falling shut. No curl deformation, no skeuomorphism — pacing, parallax, and edge shadow carry the whole fiction.
one_move: Enforce the one-hero law on Home by shipping THE SIGNED LINE: the kept line at 64–72pt with its drawn rule and seal-on-the-line as the page's only object — camera disc, hamburger, second sparkle and meta line deleted, every number demoted to one beat-19 receipt ledger, the 96pt numeral taking the page only in the post-log LANDED state. This single move creates the screenshot the founder is asking for and forces the scale discipline, the deletions, and the one-grammar rule that every other surface then inherits.
